analysis.investment_thesis: Data Patterns is one of the finest defense electronics businesses I have seen in India — 43% operating margins, 31.6% revenue CAGR, and debt-free. But at 79x P/E and P/S of 20x on a ₹708 Cr revenue base, the stock is priced as if all future success for the next 20 years is already in the price.
key_strengths: Exceptional operating margin of 43.13% — rare in Indian manufacturing, reflects genuine IP-led defense electronics franchise in IFF, radar, avionics, and EW systems
Revenue CAGR of 31.6% (FY22-FY25) with net profit CAGR of 33.1% — real, high-quality growth aligned with India's defense indigenization under Make in India
Completely debt-free (D/E 0.00) with ROCE of 19.62%, preserving equity value as the order book scales
key_risks: Free cash flow has been negative in 2 of 4 years (FY23: -₹57 Cr, FY25: -₹196 Cr) — defense contract working capital cycles create severe cash burn at scale
Promoter holding at 42.41% is below my 50% threshold and if dilution continues (QIP in FY23 spiked assets), alignment weakens
Entire revenue base of ₹708 Cr is concentrated in Indian defense procurement — a policy shift, budget cut, or DRDO/HAL internalization can devastate the order book
red_flags: P/E of 79.45x and forward P/E of 55.42x — even great businesses destroy wealth when bought at these multiples
P/S of 20.04x means you are paying ₹20 for every ₹1 of revenue — this is software-company valuation for a hardware manufacturer
Market cap of ₹19,562 Cr on ₹708 Cr revenue is completely disconnected from current business reality; requires flawless execution for 10+ years to justify
analysis.detailed_analysis: I love the Data Patterns business — it is exactly the kind of niche, IP-driven, import-substitution play in defense electronics that India needs and that can compound for decades. The margins prove moat; at 43%, no commodity business competes here. The Aatmanirbhar Bharat tailwind is real and long-lasting. However, at 79x trailing P/E, the market has already discovered this gem and priced in every possible positive outcome. My edge as an investor comes from buying before the crowd arrives, not after they've bid the stock to 20x sales. The FCF inconsistency (negative ₹196 Cr in FY25 despite ₹222 Cr net profit) signals that as orders scale, working capital requirements are intensifying — a structural feature of defense contracts that can persist for years and strain liquidity. I would want to see this at 25-30x earnings before getting excited. Until then, wonderful business, wrong price.
